paras: The beating of Alex O'Bannon was an assault on a Black man in Butte, Montana, on the night of 21 August 1900, in which he was clubbed over the head. The man first charged, Steve Hoy, was said to have tried to start a "race war," but two days later another man, Billy Berkley, pleaded guilty and was fined $15.

On the morning of 22 August, Steve Hoy appeared in the Butte police court charged with beating O'Bannon, described as "a colored man," over the head with a club the night before. According to statements made in court, Hoy had "tried to inaugurate a race war." O'Bannon showed the court his head, which the Daily Inter Mountain called "frightfully beaten," and his face was badly cut. Hoy pleaded not guilty, and his trial was set for Friday.

On 24 August, Billy Berkley, charged with beating O'Bannon, pleaded guilty in Judge Sullivan's police court and was fined $15. The paper said the plea exonerated Hoy, "who was first implicated, as he had nothing to do with the affair." Neither report gives the cause of the beating or the race of either man charged.

The only coverage found was in the Butte Daily Inter Mountain, which ran both items in its daily police-court column among cases of drunkenness, theft and street fights. The first item, under the heading "In Police Court," led with the "race war" remark but attributed it to "the statements made" rather than to the paper itself. The follow-up, two sentences long inside a column headed "Ten Dollar Bill Missing," reported the guilty plea and fine and cleared Hoy without comment on the earlier charge. No Black-press report of the beating was found.

The two reports name different assailants: the 22 August item charged Steve Hoy, while the 24 August item recorded Billy Berkley's guilty plea and said Hoy had nothing to do with it. The later report rests on a guilty plea and expressly withdraws the charge against Hoy, so it is the better evidence on who beat O'Bannon.
